clue.text: Acknowledging defeat in underwater operation

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel that runs underwater
a mission is a military or covert operation

explanation.surface: Someone concedes they have lost during a diving operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to an opponent and conceding the contest is the act of giving in, a synonym for this formal surrender.

clue.text: Page penned by hack is prominent news item

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed within it, as in a pen

parts.note: to hack is to slash or cut roughly

explanation.surface: A front-page story written by a hack journalist is big news.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is newspaper slang for the main front-page story given the biggest headline.

clue.text: Scrounger's urge to be in pub

indicators.note: the urge is placed so as to be inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A freeloader feels the urge to go to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is one who scrounges money or food from others, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Eggheads with terribly elitist leaning

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of these words are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Intellectuals are accused of a dreadfully snobbish bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is informal for intellectuals, and the intellectual class collectively has this Russian-derived name.

clue.text: Frittered paper cash getting a lot of rubbish

indicators.note: frittered suggests something broken into pieces and wasted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Banknotes wasted away end up as so much garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded junk, literally a large quantity of refuse.

clue.text: Saxon King left poor-quality meat

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century Anglo-Saxon king of Mercia

explanation.surface: An old English monarch abandoned some inferior cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the organs and entrails of an animal, regarded as cheaper, lower-grade meat.

clue.text: Sticks around being sanctimonious

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: gums as a verb means sticks with glue

explanation.surface: Someone hanging about acting holier-than-thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means self-righteously pleased with oneself, close in sense to a holier-than-thou attitude.

clue.text: Wood old golfer used in springtime

indicators.note: the golfer is put to use inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of springtime
Ben Hogan was a great American golfer of the mid-twentieth century

explanation.surface: A veteran golfer's wooden club was used in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown timber prized for furniture.

clue.text: Awful quality of Colosseum performance with singer so squiffy

indicators.note: squiffy means tipsy, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy vocalist gives a dreadful show in an ancient Roman arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' looks like a criticism of the show, but the definition is the bloodiness of gladiator fights in Rome's Colosseum.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiatorial contests were bloody, and bloodiness is the quality of being covered in gore.

clue.text: Product of light rubber that can provide what's wanted

definitions.text: Product of light rubber that can provide what's wanted

parts.words: Product of light rubber that can provide what's wanted
parts.note: rubbing an old oil lamp, a source of light, summons the wish-granting spirit of the Aladdin tale

explanation.surface: An eraser for light pencil marks gives you just what you need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light rubber' reads as a soft eraser, but it is someone who rubs a light, Aladdin's lamp, releasing the spirit who grants wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aladdin story, rubbing the lamp produces a magical being who grants whatever is desired.

clue.text: Come down stairs, missing the first

indicators.note: missing the first means the opening letter is dropped from the word for stairs

parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: Descend the staircase but skip the top step.
explanation.definitionFit: To light on or alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands.

clue.text: Such a course concerning new student? Yes and no

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a fresher is a first-year university student

explanation.surface: Is this a course for first-year students? Partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' comments on the surface: the wordplay mentions a new student, yet a course of this kind is for those who studied before.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course updates or revives earlier training, so the answer describes such a course.

clue.text: Sent back fish, king rejected shellfish

indicators.note: sent back tells us the remaining letters are returned in reverse order
rejected means the king is thrown out of the fish

parts.note: pollacks are fish of the cod family
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A diner returns the fish, and the king refuses the seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallop is a bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped shell.

clue.text: Stocking up with booze, say, precluding a being abed late

indicators.note: precluding means shutting out, so the letter is left out

parts.note: laying in supplies such as drink means stocking up

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles drink and then stays in bed long into the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual hour is a lie-in, so remaining abed is this phrase.

clue.text: Hunter: I'd do so with organisation

definitions.text: Hunter: I'd do so with organisation

indicators.note: with organisation means the letters are arranged into an orderly new form

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A huntsman declares he'd take part as part of an organised hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a hunter would say he would follow the hounds with an organised hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow foxhounds on horseback is what a hunter does, exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: They wrought rich goals

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: These people created wealthy aims.
explanation.walkthrough: The rich few who rule are the 'They' who might well work towards rich goals.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to a small ruling group of tycoons, the people who achieved rich goals.

clue.text: Spite could be result of being this far from the beaten track

parts.words: Spite could be result of being this
parts.note: a ski run made off, or disordered, gives the letters of spite

explanation.surface: Malice might come of straying from the usual path.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: a piste that is 'off', jumbled, could become SPITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing away from groomed runs is literally away from the trodden path.

clue.text: Filling in alien visa generally needs picture

indicators.note: the answer fills the inside of these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: Completing a foreign national's visa form usually requires a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine or visualise it, a synonym of envisage.

clue.text: Clue for police to identify criminal makes an impression

parts.note: to finger someone is slang for identifying them as the culprit
prints means presses a mark or impression

explanation.surface: A detective's crucial evidence helps nail the offender and leaves a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks left by fingertips at a crime scene are classic evidence for detectives.

clue.text: Make declaration in top cricket match

parts.note: at means in, as in at home
a Test is an international cricket match, the top level of the game

explanation.surface: A statement is made during a major cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to state formally or bear witness to something.

clue.text: Meal for group about right

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the group surrounds the letter

parts.note: a bunch is a group

explanation.surface: Food served to a party about the correct size.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Constable, perhaps, represented by a penetrating playwright

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the letter enters the playwright

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British dramatist

explanation.surface: A police officer appears in a play by a sharp writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests a policeman, but it is John Constable, the English landscape artist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape artist, an example of one who paints.

clue.text: Turner that looks the same hung upside-down

indicators.text: that looks the same hung upside-down
indicators.note: in a down entry, reading bottom to top gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that spins looks unchanged when inverted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' hints at the painter, but it is anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: A superior person giving encouragement

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: Someone of higher standing offers support.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist, so one who does so is named for that verb.

clue.text: Still absorbing first fact

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the short piece goes inside

parts.note: static means still or motionless
1st, written IST in crosswords, means first

explanation.surface: A motionless thing taking in the first piece of information.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a numerical piece of data, a single fact expressed as a figure.

clue.text: The woman embraced by an Irish leader once

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the woman sits inside

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A lady hugged by a former Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Ahern was Taoiseach, the Irish prime minister, from 1997 to 2008.

clue.text: Business leader out of the City

parts.note: ex means out of, from Latin
EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A boss leaving the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec is short for executive, a senior manager running a company.

clue.text: Bad-tempered fellow from Scottish shire with penny in bag

indicators.note: in places the shire and the coin inside the word for bag

parts.note: to bag is to catch
Ross-shire is a former county in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A grumpy man from the Highlands with a coin in his pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an irritable, grumpy person, an old informal term.
